STUDENT ARTICLE BY SIDDHI GAWADE: Memory-First Computing: Why
Processing Is Moving Toward Data
Not long ago, improving computer performance meant making processors faster. Each
generation delivered higher clock speeds, more cores, and powerful GPUs. Today's systems tell a
different story. Modern workloads such as AI training, big data analytics, and real time applications
spend more time moving data than processing it. Constant transfers between memory and
processors consume time and energy, creating a bottleneck that faster processors alone cannot
solve.

I am Samudragupta Jejurkar, a Computer Engineering student at Vidyalankar Institute of
Technology, and my academic sojourn here has been nothing less than transformative.
From my very first day, I was enthralled by the department's culture of intellectual rigor,
dynamic pedagogy, and its ceaseless commitment to shaping students into consummate
professionals.
The Computer Engineering Department at VIT is not merely an academic unit; it is an
intellectual crucible that fosters innovation, nurtures leadership, and refines character. Under
the sagacious stewardship of Dr. Ravindra Sangle, our Head of Department, the environment
has always been one of encouragement and excellence.

INSTITUTE LEVEL & AGAINST CAP (ACAP) ADMISSIONS POLICY & GUIDELINES

1. Admission Categories:
Institute Level admissions are divided into two primary categories:
a) Against CAP (ACAP): Seats remaining vacant after the Centralized Admission Process (CAP Round IV) conducted by the State CET Cell.
b) Institute Level (IL): Up to a maximum quota of 20% of the sanctioned intake of the program.

2. Eligibility Criteria:
Candidates who have registered online, completed document verification, and received confirmation from a registered Scrutiny Center (SC) are eligible for Institute Level and ACAP admissions.

MISSION OF THE DEPARTMENT
1. To evolve a curriculum emphasizing strong engineering fundamentals with flexibility to choose advanced courses and gain exposure to Information Technology tools and techniques.
2. Encourage a teaching-learning process in which highly competent faculty share a symbiotic association with the institutes of repute.
3. Facilitate creation and dissemination of knowledge through a digitally-enabled learning environment.
4. Develop academic and infrastructural facilities with modern equipment and other learning resources and encourage reciprocal sharing with other institutes through networking.

PROGRAMME EDUCATIONAL OBJECTIVES (PEO)
PEO 1: To provide students with strong foundational and technical knowledge in Information Technology.
PEO 2: Graduates should analyze real-life problems and design technically sound, economically feasible and socially acceptable solutions, engaging in entrepreneurship.
PEO 3: Graduates should exhibit professionalism, ethics, teamwork, social awareness, and lifelong learning to continuously improve professionally and technically.
Primary objective of the department is to develop competent, ethical, and industry-ready professionals through quality education, research, and innovation.
